messages:
anna: Ran a quick nsys on the latest runtime with INT8/FP8 mixed paths — seeing a huge dequant/quant overhead when the kernel selector flips mid-request. timeline attached: https://perf.company/trace/1764123456 :thinking_face:
matt: Can you paste the lightweight nsys summary? Is it happening during KV lookups or at the matmul kernels?
anna: Short summary from nsys CLI:
```
GPU activities: matmul_fp8 ~ 35ms total, matmul_int8 ~ 28ms total
dequant kernels (fp8->f16) ~ 22ms (many small launches)
quant kernels (f16->int8) ~ 12ms
host memcpy small spikes during KV restore
```
Looks like dequant is almost as expensive as the matmul when we switch formats.
sara: That matches what I saw — when sequence lengths vary in the same batch the kernel selector will choose FP8 for some tokens and INT8 for others, which forces per-step dequant/quant around the KV plumbing. KV cache ends up getting re-encoded repeatedly.
kev: Perfetto view: the NVTX ranges show alternating color bands every few micro-batches — kernel switching overhead corresponds to lots of tiny memcpy + re-encode calls. link: https://perfetto.company/ui/trace/1764123456 (zoom to 0:02-0:04)
perf-bot: Scheduled perf run 1764123460 completed. Artifacts: s3://perfruns/1764123460/nsystrace.qdrep
matt: Hypothesis: our kernel selector is too eager to pick FP8 for raw GEMM perf without considering amortized cost of format conversions + KV traffic. Also batching heuristic is producing many small micro-batches (batch_size distribution skewed to 1-4).
anna: Agreed. Suggested quick experiments:
1) Force INT8-only model path (disable fp8 kernels)
2) Force FP8-only path (disable int8 kernels)
3) Enable "sticky-kv" so KV stays in the same encoding for a request
4) Run with continuous_batching off
kev: I captured an nsys capture with nvtx markers: the dequant kernel is launched ~120x vs matmul ~18x for a 20-token run — that's the root cause. Attaching snippet:
```
# nvtx ranges (abridged)
[step_0] matmul_int8 1.2ms
[step_0] dequant_fp8 0.8ms
[step_1] matmul_fp8 1.6ms
[step_1] dequant_fp8 0.9ms
...
```
Small launches kill the GPU throughput.
sara: Also check our pack_kv path. If we pack/unpack KV per-step we reformat memory which forces host-gpu memcpy. Two ideas: keep KV in a canonical GPU format across steps, or add a conversion cache so we only convert when the encoding actually changes for a given KV shard.
matt: I'll try a quick patch: prevent kernel switching within a request by selecting the cheaper-of-two stable format when micro-batch count < threshold. Pseudoconfig below:
```
{"kernel_selection": "stable_with_threshold", "micro_batch_threshold": 8, "sticky_kv": true, "fused_dequant": true}
```
Should reduce churn.
anna: Can you also try enabling fused_dequant on FP8 path? That should collapse the separate dequant kernel into the GEMM pipeline and reduce launches.
matt: Will run two passes: (A) fused_dequant=true + sticky_kv=true (B) stable_selection disabled (control). Scheduling runs now.
perf-bot: Run started: perfrun-1764123500 (A) and perfrun-1764123530 (B)
kev: Quick note — remember to profile with `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,nvtx` and capture device-side timestamps. Host sampling adds noise.
sara: Also add a perf regression watch: compare tokens/sec and p99 latency. If fused_dequant reduces kernel launches but increases compute time slightly, net effect may still be wins.
anna: Good. If experiments confirm, we should: 1) add a runtime flag to avoid cross-format kernel switching mid-request, 2) add conversion caching for KV, 3) enable fused_dequant for FP8 path by default behind a runtime toggle.
matt: Running now, will post nsys summaries + flamegraphs here when done.
anna: Thanks — if anyone sees severe accuracy drops in FP8-only run, call it out. We'll keep the eval harness running to validate logits.
kev: FYI initial A run shows 2.6x drop in dequant kernel launches and ~30% improvement in tokens/sec. Still collecting full metrics. :thumbsup:
sara: Awesome. Keep an eye on memory impact when keeping KV sticky (it increases GPU memory for encoded KV), but should be fine for our 8k tests.
anna: Closing loop later today after both runs finish. If results hold, plan patch + small rollout on dedicated clusters. :rocket:
